branchName.instructions:
Use lowercase <type>/<short-kebab-description>, ideally 2-5 words after the slash.

Type is either a change type (feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, chore, test) or the area the work lives in (ui, network, simulation).

Describe the change itself, not the agent, model, ticket or conversation that produced it. Personal experiments use mb/<description>.

Examples: ui/ingame-theme, chore/add-agents-md, simulation/audit-fixes, network/draft-reliability, fix/drag-proxy-flash

commitMessage.instructions:
Use Conventional Commits with no scope, matching this repo's history: '<type>: <lowercase imperative summary>', where type is feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, chore or test. Keep the first line under 72 characters when practical.

Use 'done: <task title>' only when the commit completes a Notion task.

For larger or non-obvious changes, add a short body explaining why, and any important behavioural or architectural effect.

Describe what changed, not how it was produced: no narration of the agent's process, and no 'Generated by AI' style lines in the subject or body. A Co-Authored-By trailer is fine.

Examples: fix: heal shrine occupants on their own interval; refactor: share production district arrival dispatch; test: add deterministic claiming coverage

pullRequest.instructions:
Use a concise title that describes the completed change. Use these sections when relevant, and omit empty ones:

## Summary
A few bullets: what changed and why.

## Changes
Important implementation changes, focused on behaviour and architecture rather than a file list.

## Determinism / networking
State explicitly whether Simulation/ was touched and needs determinism review, and whether networking changed and needs lockstep/desync review.

## Testing
What was actually run (dotnet test, scripts/compile-check.ps1, scripts/sim-guard.ps1) and the result. Never claim a check that was not run.

## Unity Setup
Required Inspector assignments, prefab, scene or serialized-field changes, missing .meta files, or other Editor steps.

## Risks / manual verification
What needs verifying in the Unity Editor or a playtest, with particular attention to deterministic simulation, networking, serialization, game-state transitions and Unity lifecycle.

Keep the PR focused. Keep AI tooling out of the substance; a single attribution footer line is fine.
